Fuchs.definition_html:
1. nprop-nfemmascnamesurnstrongnon-lemma(wty-de-en)
    • Grammar
      Fuchs m (strong, genitive Fuchses, plural Füchse, diminutive Füchslein n or Füchschen n, feminine Füchsin)
      Etymology
      From Middle High German vuhs, from Old High German fuhs, from Proto-West Germanic *fuhs, from Proto-Germanic *fuhsaz, from Proto-Indo-European *púḱsos (“the tailed one”), from *puḱ- (“tail”). Cognate with English fox, Sanskrit पुच्छ (púccha).
      1. fox (animal)
        1 example
        Fuchs, du hast die Gans gestohlen. Gib sie wieder her!
        Fox, you've stolen the goose. Give it back here!
      2. inf
        a clever or cunning person, sly fox
        1 example
        Er ist ein ganz schöner Fuchs.
        He is quite the sly fox.
      3. inf
        redhead (a red-haired person)
        1 example
        Unser Paul ist ja ein kleiner Fuchs.
        Our Paul is a little redhead.
      4. sports
        chestnut, sorrel horse (horse with a reddish-brown coat, mane and tail)
      5. pledge (prospective member of a fraternity)
      6. slmilpolit
        a new recruit
      7. the ace of diamonds in Doppelkopf, where it earns a side of players an extra point if they win it from the other side
        1 example
        Ich hatte nur vier Trümpfe und darunter beide Füchse.
        I had only four trumps and among them were both aces of diamonds.
      8. milpolit
        a tank Transportpanzer Fuchs
      9. arch
        a form of sunscald on hops
      10. a fox in radiosport foxhunt
      11. obs
        any gold coin
      12. biolentom
        tortoiseshell
      Wiktionary | Kaikki

Straße.definition_html:
1. nfemnon-lemma(wty-de-en)
    • Grammar
      Straße f (genitive Straße, plural Straßen, diminutive Sträßchen n or Sträßlein n)
      Etymology
      Etymology tree
      Proto-Indo-European *ster-
      Proto-Indo-European *sterh₃-
      Proto-Indo-European *-tós
      Proto-Indo-European *str̥h₃tós
      Proto-Italic *strātos
      Latin strātus
      Latin via strātaellip.
      Late Latin strātabor.
      Proto-West Germanic *strātu
      Old High German strāȥa
      Middle High German strāȥe
      German Straße
      Inherited from Middle High German strāȥe, from Old High German strāȥa, from Proto-West Germanic *strātu (“street”), from Latin (via) strata.
      Sense 6 (“strait”) is a calque of Middle Low German strâte, itself a phono-semantic matching of Middle English streit, from Old French estreit (“narrow”), from unrelated Latin strictus.
      1. street; road (a way wide enough to be passable for vehicles, generally paved, in or outside a settlement)
        3 examples
        Das Kind überquerte die Straße.
        The child crossed the street.
        Diese Straße führt nach Kirchdorf.
        This road goes to Kirchdorf.
        Die Straße ist für den Verkehr gesperrt.
        The street is closed for traffic.
      2. carriageway (the part of a road or street used by vehicles, excluding the pavement, etc.)
      3. fig
        public, any area accessible to anyone
      4. fig
        general public, using the locale to describe people not part of a specific group
      5. the streets, areas or groups of people of no income or criminal affiliation, or the leading of a life associated with these
      6. strait (channel of water)
      7. poker
        straight
      Wiktionary | Kaikki

ansehen.definition_html:
1. vstrong(wty-de-en)
    • Grammar
      ansehen (class 5 strong, third-person singular present sieht an, past tense sah an, past participle angesehen, past subjunctive sähe an, auxiliary haben)
      Etymology
      an- + sehen
      1. vrvt
        to look at, to have a look at (taking in information in doing so)
        1 example
        Sieh dir diese riesige Tomate an.
        Have a look at this huge tomato.
      2. vt
        to look at (especially a person; implying eye contact or direction of gaze without analyzing)
        2 examples
        Sie sah ihn erstaunt an.
        She looked at him in astonishment.
        Sarah ist wunderschön anzusehen.
        Sarah is beautiful to look at.
      3. vtfig
        to regard, to consider, to look on (something in a certain way or having a certain quality)
        1 example
        Ich sehe ihren Schutz als unsere Verantwortung an.
        I see their protection as our responsibility.
      4. vt
        to watch (a movie, a television program, sports, etc)
        1 example
        Siehst du gerne Fußball im Fernsehen an?
        Do you like to watch soccer/football on television?
      5. vdt
        to notice, to be able to tell (a quality based on the look of someone/something); to be apparent (with subject and object switched)
        1 example
        Man sieht dir an, dass du zwei Tage lang nicht geschlafen hast.
        It's obvious just from looking at you that you haven't slept in two days.
      Wiktionary | Kaikki

schön.definition_html:
1. adjadvnon-lemma(wty-de-en)
    • Grammar
      schön (strong nominative masculine singular schöner, comparative schöner, superlative am schönsten)
      Etymology
      Inherited from Middle High German schœne, from Old High German scōni, from Proto-West Germanic *skaunī, from Proto-Germanic *skauniz.
      1. beautiful, lovely, pretty, handsome
        2 examples
        Der Sonnenuntergang am Strand war wirklich schön.
        The sunset on the beach was really beautiful.
        Nowhere is there a land more beautiful than ours at this time [or in this age]...
      2. good, great, splendid
      3. nice, pleasant
        1 example
        Am liebsten entfloh sie dem allem in den großen Garten. Da verbrachte sie ihre schönsten Stunden.
        She liked best to escape from all of that into the big garden. There she spent her most pleasant hours.
      Wiktionary | Kaikki
